claim_en: SEVEN ALTARS, SEVEN BULLS, SEVEN RAMS — THREE TIMES; A BULL AND A RAM ON THE ALTAR — FOUR TIMES, AND THE TRANSLATION ADDS 'EVERY'. 'Build me here SEVEN ALTARS and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams' (23:1) — the phrase at 23:1, 14, 29 and 'the seven altars' at 23:4; the parser reads 7, 7, 7 here and at 23:29; three stands, twenty-one altars, forty-two beasts (the exam's Nazir 23b reads Ruth out of them); 'Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on THE altar' (23:2) — the clause four times (23:2, 4, 14, 30), singular in the ink; ONKELOS 'on EVERY altar' at all four (computed, cut from the shelf's bytes).
middah: ink (the sevens and the altar-clause counted; the translation's 'every' cut)

source: Onkelos Num 23:3; Onkelos Num 23:4; Onkelos Num 23:5; Onkelos Num 23:6
claim_en: STAND BY YOUR BURNT OFFERING; PERHAPS THE LORD WILL CHANCE TO MEET ME — THE VERB OF 'THE GOD OF THE HEBREWS HAS MET WITH US'; A BARE HEIGHT, ALONE; GOD MET BALAAM; THE LORD PUT A WORD IN HIS MOUTH — THE PROPHET-CLAUSE'S FIRST EXEMPLAR. 'Stand by your burnt offering and I will go; perhaps the LORD will CHANCE to meet me' (23:3) — the chance-verb (karah) at 23:3, 4, 15, 16 is Moses' word to Pharaoh, 'the God of the Hebrews has MET with us' (Exod 3:18, 5:3), the servant's 'cause it to happen' at the well (Gen 24:12), and 'a CHANCE of the night' (Deut 23:11) — the shelf hears the impurity in the prophet's word; 'he went to A BARE HEIGHT' — the word's one Torah seat, Onkelos 'ALONE' (computed, cut); 'and GOD MET Balaam' (23:4) — God here, the LORD at 23:16; 'the seven altars I have ARRANGED, and I have offered up' — Balaam claims the offering in the first person; 'and THE LORD PUT A WORD IN BALAAM'S MOUTH' (23:5, one seat; 23:16 'in his mouth') — the clause of the prophet like Moses, 'I will put My words in his mouth' (Deut 18:18), of Jeremiah's call (1:9) and Isaiah's (51:16): the definition's first narrative exemplar is a gentile (computed); 'return to Balak and thus you shall speak'; 'behold, he was standing by his burnt offering' (23:6, and 23:17). Onkelos: 'met' → a WORD from before the LORD met (cut).
middah: ink (the chance-verb's seats, the height's one seat and the mouth-clause's kin computed)

check.note: 'will chance to meet' — the karah-verb, Exodus 3:18's and Deuteronomy 23:11's

claim_en: HE TOOK UP HIS PARABLE — SEVEN TIMES, THE PARABLE-TELLERS' WORD PAID; FROM ARAM; CURSE JACOB, DENOUNCE ISRAEL — THE THIRD ROOT AND THE SIX PAIRS; HOW SHALL I CURSE WHOM EL HAS NOT CURSED — EL'S EIGHT. 'And he TOOK UP HIS PARABLE and said' (23:7) — the clause SEVEN times (23:7, 18; 24:3, 15, 20, 21, 23); the mashal-noun's Torah seats are 21:27's PARABLE-TELLERS, these seven and Deut 28:37 (Gen 45:8, 26 'ruler' the homograph; seventy-one in the Bible) — sitting 6's owed row paid: the book's first parable the poets' of Heshbon, its next seven Balaam's (computed); 'from ARAM Balak led me, from the mountains of the east' — Aram's one seat in the portion, Deut 23:5's 'Pethor of Aram-naharaim' the retelling; 'come, curse Jacob for me, and come, DENOUNCE Israel' — the third curse-root (za'am) enters; JACOB and ISRAEL paired in six oracle-verses (23:7, 10, 21, 23; 24:5, 17); 'how shall I curse whom EL has not cursed, and how shall I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced' (23:8, one seat) — EL with the tsere (the long e vowel) stands EIGHT times in the two oracle chapters (23:8, 19, 22, 23; 24:4, 8, 16, 23) and nowhere in 22 or 25; 'kabboh' the qabab-root's third token, the alcove's consonants (computed on the points). Onkelos: 'denounce' → DRIVE OUT (cut).
middah: ink (the mashal-word's seats, the pairs and the names' census computed)

check.note: 'his parable' — the parable-tellers' word, taken up seven times

claim_en: A PEOPLE THAT DWELLS ALONE — THE LEPER'S TWO WORDS; WHO HAS COUNTED THE DUST OF JACOB — ABRAHAM'S CLAUSE ANSWERED; THE FOURTH PART — REBA'S CONSONANTS; THE DEATH OF THE UPRIGHT; MY END. 'From the top of the rocks I see it, from the hills I behold it' (23:9) — the two verbs return at 24:17; 'behold, a people that DWELLS ALONE' (one seat) — the alone-word's Torah four: THE LEPER 'alone shall he dwell' (Lev 13:46), this, Moses' 'the LORD alone led him' and 'Israel dwells in safety alone' (Deut 32:12, 33:28); Lamentations' 'how she sits alone' the run (computed); Onkelos: 'alone, DESTINED TO INHERIT THE WORLD... not JUDGED TO DESTRUCTION' (cut); 'WHO HAS COUNTED THE DUST OF JACOB' (23:10, one seat) answers Abraham's 'if a man can COUNT the DUST of the earth, your seed too shall be counted' (Gen 13:16); 'THE FOURTH PART of Israel' (rova with the cholam, the long o vowel) carries the consonants of the quarter-hin (Exod 29:40, with the segol), of REBA the Midianite king killed beside Balaam (31:8) and of the bestiality-verb (Lev 18:23) — the parser silent, right (the exam's Niddah 31a reads the couplings); Onkelos 'one of the FOUR CAMPS' (cut); 'let my soul die the death of the upright, and let my END be like his' (one seat) — the end-word three times in the portion (23:10, 24:14, 24:20); he dies by the sword (computed).
middah: E10 (the repeated expression — the leper's 'alone' and Abraham's 'count the dust' at the oracle; the rova homographs by the points)

check.note: 'my end' — like the upright's; he dies by the sword

claim_en: WHAT HAVE YOU DONE TO ME — THE ASS'S QUESTION; THAT I KEEP TO SPEAK; ONLY ITS EDGE; THE FIELD OF ZOPHIM AT THE TOP OF PISGAH — MOSES' DEATH-VIEW; I WILL BE MET. 'What have you done to me? to curse my enemies I took you, and you have surely blessed' (23:11) — the ass's 'what have I done to you' (22:28) turned; 'what the LORD puts in my mouth, that I KEEP to speak' (23:12) — the formula's fourth, the verb 'keep'; 'come to another place: ONLY ITS EDGE you will see, all of it you will not see' (23:13, one seat) — 22:41's 'edge of the people', the restrictor (efes) its third seat; 'he took him to the field of Zophim, to THE TOP OF PISGAH' (23:14) — 'the field of Zophim' one seat; 'the top of Pisgah' four: the well-song's station (21:20), Balaam's second stand, 'go up to the top of Pisgah' (Deut 3:27) and Moses' death-climb (34:1) — the seer's lookout is the leader's last view (computed); Onkelos 'the field of THE WATCHERS, the top of THE HEIGHT' (cut); 'stand here by your burnt offering, and I will be MET there' (23:15) — the chance-verb's reflexive, one seat; Onkelos 'I will GO as far as there' (cut).
middah: ink (the formula's fourth, the restrictor's third seat and Pisgah's four computed)

check.note: 'Pisgah' — the top, Moses' death-view and Balaam's stand

claim_en: THE LORD MET BALAAM; RISE, BALAK, SON OF ZIPPOR — THE ARCHAIC FORM; GOD IS NOT A MAN THAT HE SHOULD LIE — SAMUEL'S VERSE OVER AGAG; THE TRANSLATION'S SERMON; I HAVE RECEIVED TO BLESS. 'And THE LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth' (23:16) — 23:4 said God; 'what has the LORD spoken?' (23:17) — the king asks by the Name; 'rise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, SON OF Zippor' (23:18) — 'his son' for 'son of' (beno), the archaic construct three times in the oracles (23:18, 24:3, 24:15), Zippor defective (computed on the points); 'EL IS NOT A MAN THAT HE SHOULD LIE, NOR A SON OF MAN THAT HE SHOULD REPENT' (23:19, one seat) — SAMUEL restates it to Saul over Agag, 'the Eternity of Israel does not lie nor repent, for He is not a man to repent' (1 Sam 15:29) — in the chapter of the king 24:7 names ('higher than Agag'), whose name Esther gives Haman the Agagite (computed); ONKELOS expands the twelve-word verse into a twenty-seven-word sermon — 'not like the words of the sons of men is the Word of God... He says and does, and all His Word is fulfilled' (cut from the shelf's bytes); 'to bless I have RECEIVED; He has blessed, and I cannot turn it back' (23:20, one seat, six words); Onkelos 'blessings I have received, and I will bless ISRAEL' (cut).
middah: ink (the archaic form by the points, Samuel's restatement and Agag's seats computed; the translation's sermon cut)

check.note: 'that He should repent' — the clause Samuel restates over Agag

claim_en: NO INIQUITY BEHELD IN JACOB; THE SHOUT OF A KING — THE TERUAH MADE THE SHEKHINAH; EL BRINGS THEM OUT OF EGYPT — ONE LETTER FROM 24:8; THE WILD-OX'S HORNS JOSEPH'S. 'He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, nor seen toil in Israel' (23:21, one seat); 'the LORD his God is with him, and THE SHOUT OF A KING is among him' (one seat) — the teruah-word's Torah seven: the trumpets' (10:5-6), the jubilee's (Lev 25:9), Rosh Hashanah's (Lev 23:24, Num 29:1), the Midian war's (31:6) and this; ONKELOS renders it 'the SHEKHINAH of their king among them' where at 10:5 and 29:1 the same noun is 'a WAIL' (sitting 3's find) — one Hebrew noun, the Presence at Balaam and the wailing at the trumpets (computed, cut); 'EL brings THEM out of Egypt, like the horns of the wild-ox to Him' (23:22) — the verse returns at 24:8 with ONE LETTER changed, 'brings HIM out' (a mem for a vav); the horn-word's four seats (Job 22:25, Ps 95:4); the wild-ox's horns are JOSEPH's in Moses' blessing (Deut 33:17) (computed); Onkelos 'STRENGTH AND EXALTATION are His' — the beast dropped (cut).
middah: ink (the teruah-word's seven and its two renderings, the one-letter delta and the wild-ox's seats computed)

check.note: 'and the shout' of a king — the teruah rendered the Shekhinah

claim_en: NO DIVINATION IN JACOB — THE SERPENT'S WORD IN THE DIVINER'S MOUTH; NO SORCERY IN ISRAEL; WHAT HAS EL WROUGHT; A PEOPLE RISES LIKE A LIONESS — JUDAH'S BEASTS IN THE OTHER ORDER; THE BLOOD OF THE SLAIN. 'For there is no DIVINATION in Jacob and no SORCERY in Israel' (23:23; 'no sorcery in Israel' one seat) — nachash (divination, with the patach) is THE SERPENT's consonants: 24:1's 'divinations' (nechashim) and 21:6's 'the serpents' (ha-nechashim) share consonants AND vowels, told by the article and the story alone; Laban 'I have divined' (Gen 30:27), Joseph's cup (44:5, 15), Lev 19:26 and Deut 18:10 its ban — the diviner (22:7; Josh 13:22) declares no divining in Israel (computed on the points); Onkelos 'the DIVINERS do not wish good to the house of Jacob' (cut); 'at this time it shall be said to Jacob and to Israel, what has EL wrought' (one seat); 'behold, a people rises like a LIONESS and lifts itself like a LION' (23:24) — Judah's two beasts (Gen 49:9) in the other order, 24:9 giving them as Jacob had them; the exam's Berakhot 12b names this clause the reason the portion was nearly fixed in the Shema; 'it shall not lie down until it eats prey and drinks the BLOOD OF THE SLAIN' (one seat) — the slain-word of 19:16; Onkelos 'inherits THE WEALTH OF THE NATIONS' (cut).
middah: ink (the serpent-and-divination homograph by the points and the beasts' order computed; the translation's readings cut)

check.note: 'the slain' — whose blood the lion drinks; 19:16's word

claim_en: NEITHER CURSE NOR BLESS; ALL THE LORD SPEAKS, THAT I DO — THE FORMULA'S FIFTH; ANOTHER PLACE; THE TOP OF PEOR THAT LOOKS DOWN ON THE JESHIMON — 21:20'S CLAUSE WITH PEOR FOR PISGAH, THE THIRD STAND THE GOD OF THE SIN. 'Neither curse him at all nor bless him at all' (23:25) — the qabab-root's seventh and eighth tokens; 'all that the LORD speaks, that I DO' (23:26) — the formula's fifth, 22:20's 'do' returning; 'come, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will be right in the eyes of God' (23:27) — the third stand; 'Balak took Balaam to THE TOP OF PEOR that LOOKS DOWN on the Jeshimon' (23:28, one seat) — 21:20's station reads 'the top of Pisgah that looks down on the Jeshimon': the same clause, Peor for Pisgah — Balaam's three stands are Israel's last three stations (Bamoth, Pisgah, Peor), and the third is the god of 25:3; Peor's thirteen seats run from this lookout through the sin (25:3, 5, 18; 31:16) to MOSES' GRAVE 'opposite Beth-peor' (Deut 34:6), Joshua's 'is the iniquity of Peor too little' (22:17), the Psalm's 'sacrifices of the dead' (106:28) (computed); Onkelos drops Peor's name — 'the top of the height... Beth-jeshimon' (cut).

claim_en: SEVEN ALTARS, SEVEN BULLS, SEVEN RAMS — THE SECOND SAYING VERBATIM; BALAK DID AS BALAAM SAID; THE TRANSLATION'S VERB PLENE HERE, DEFECTIVE AT 23:1. 'Build me here seven altars and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams' (23:29) — 23:1 word for word, the parser 7, 7, 7 at both; 'Balak did as Balaam had SAID, and offered up a bull and a ram on the altar' (23:30) — 23:2 said 'as Balaam had SPOKEN'; the altar-clause's fourth seat, Onkelos 'on every altar' the fourth time; and the translation's 'prepare' is spelled PLENE at 23:29 and DEFECTIVE at 23:1 (cut from the two rows' bytes; computed).
